God noun

classical

Traupman 256, 259
Vulg. Gen. 1.1

Deus, Deī m.

noun, second declension

God; a god

The one God, and, with a small letter, any god; the gods are dī (also deī). The vocative is Deus (Deus, Deus meus, Ps. 62 (63), 2). Deō grātiās, thank God; Deō volente, God willing (Traupman).

Examples

  • In prīncipiō creāvit Deus caelum et terram.

    In the beginning God created heaven and earth.Vulg. Gen. 1.1

  • Deō grātiās.

    Thank God.Traupman 259

  • Deō volente.

    God willing.Traupman 256

See also the Lord, the Holy Spirit, the Trinity, heaven, faith.

SourcesLewis & Short: deus
